world.bio: I am a second-year nursing student at a university in western Sydney, originally from Pokhara, Nepal. On weekends I clean houses and small offices with two classmates to pay rent. I like checklists: every job has a printed sheet, with tick boxes for each room. We have never had a complaint about missed spots.
skills_assets: Nursing student with first aid and manual handling certificates
A weekend cleaning team of three (me and two classmates): we do end-of-lease and regular home cleaning around Parramatta and Auburn
A set of printed checklists for kitchen, bathroom, bedroom, balcony
Our own equipment: two vacuums, a steam cleaner, a box of eco-friendly products
A WhatsApp group of 40 clients and neighbours who refer us

projects.name: Cleaning side income
projects.text: Three of us split the jobs on Saturday and Sunday. Typical rate is $180 to $260 per house depending on size, split three ways. Last month we did 14 jobs. I keep a spreadsheet with hours, pay, and who did what. The hard part is that jobs have to fit into Saturday and Sunday only, because weekdays are lectures and clinical placement. Many clients ask for a Friday evening or a Monday morning, I have to say no.

projects.name: Clinical placement preparation
projects.text: Starting October 12 I have a three-week placement at a hospital in Westmead on a surgical ward. Early shifts start at 6:30. I need to buy new work shoes and prepare a reflective journal template. My supervisor said keeping notes every day is the best way to pass.

notes.text: Saturday we cleaned a three-bedroom in Granville. The owner had left a note on the fridge saying 'please do not move the plants.' We moved the plants to dust and put them back exactly the same. I took a photo before and after, just in case.

Called mum in Pokhara. She asked if I am eating enough dal bhat. I said yes, even though most days it's instant noodles. She told me Dad's knee is hurting again. I said I'd send some money after the next pay. She said no, no, you need it for rent. We always go around this circle.
Anatomy quiz on Wednesday. I know the cranial nerves but I keep mixing up the branches of the facial nerve. Made a mnemonic: 'Two Zebras Bit My Cousin.' It works, but I feel silly telling it.

Checked my work hours spreadsheet again. I am close to my fortnightly limit. Last fortnight I did 46 hours between cleaning and the lab assistant shift. It is too close. I have been warned once by the uni international office about going over, and I do not want a second one. I need to be careful every week.
Cricket on Sunday evening with the Nepali students society. We lost by 12 runs, but the samosas afterwards were excellent. A guy named Binod brought homemade achar. I took a jar home.
My roommate moved out. Rent will go up by $60 a week unless I find someone new. Posted a listing on Gumtree. Two replies already, one of them seems odd. I will meet in a public place.

One of the clients, Mrs. Henderson, gave us a thank-you card with $20 inside. She said we're the only cleaners who don't talk on the phone while working. I put the card on the fridge. It is nice to be seen.
Watched a YouTube video about how nurses chart on night shifts. Took notes. Realized I need to improve my handwriting, because mine looks like a seismograph.
Cleaned two houses on Saturday. Tired. Studied in the train on the way home. I fell asleep and missed my station by two stops. At least I woke up before the end of the line.

messages.text:
Anil: Did you see the roster for next weekend?
Me: Yes. We have two jobs on Saturday, one on Sunday morning.
Anil: Can I swap to Sunday only?
Me: Yes, but then Rahul and I take both Saturday ones.

Rahul: A client wants a Friday evening clean. I said no.
Me: Good, we can't.
Rahul: She said she will pay extra.
Me: Still no. The visa.

Mum: Come home for Dashain?
Me: I can't, I have placement.
Mum: We will light a candle for you.
Me: Thank you, Ama.

Mrs. Henderson: Are you available Saturday morning?
Me: Yes, at nine.
Mrs. Henderson: Please bring the steam cleaner.
Me: Of course.

Ms. Lee: Please bring the reflective journal template on the first day.
Me: I will. Do you prefer digital or paper?
Ms. Lee: Paper, with dates and times.
Me: Understood.

calendar.event: Start of clinical placement, Westmead, 6:30 am

relations.about: Classmates and the two other members of the cleaning team. Anil is very reliable, Rahul sometimes oversleeps.
In Pokhara. Dad runs a small trekking equipment shop; the family relies partly on remittance.
A client who has become a kind of local grandmother.

constraints: All paid work must stay within the fortnightly hour limit
Only Saturday and Sunday are available for cleaning
Placement shifts start early, so Sunday evenings must be free to sleep
No physically unsafe jobs (heavy lifting, ladders above two metres)
sensitive: Close to the hours cap on my student visa and was warned once; fear of losing the visa
Rent is tight and the roommate moved out
Sends money home when possible, which stretches the budget
